CHIEF COMPLAINT
Ankle injury

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Jerry is a 45-year-old male who presents with a right ankle injury sustained while playing basketball with his son at the courts. While going up for a shot, his son collided with him and the patient landed awkwardly, rolling and twisting his ankle. The patient reports pain on the outside of the ankle with visible bruising and swelling. He has had trouble walking and reports the ankle does not feel stable. The patient recently returned to working out and has been in a good exercise routine, which he is concerned about disrupting. He also mentions that he has volunteered to coach starting in April.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Meloxicam prescribed during this visit.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works from home. He plays basketball and has recently returned to working out at the gym. He lives with his family and has dogs. He is volunteering to coach basketball starting in April.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Lateral ankle swelling noted. Exquisite tenderness over lateral aspect of ankle. Some tenderness over medial deltoid region. Skin intact with no breakdown. Brisk capillary refill. No malalignment. Patient able to stand on ankle but has difficulty walking due to pain and feeling of instability.

RESULTS
X-ray of right ankle (AP, lateral, and oblique views): Displaced lateral malleolus fracture at Weber C level. No medial or posterior malleolar fractures. Fracture location is unstable.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Lateral malleolar fracture of right ankle. Recommended treatment is surgical intervention with plate and screw fixation. Patient will require crutches. Expected recovery time is approximately three months out of activity, though patient may continue coaching starting in April. Ice ankle and keep elevated; patient able to elevate regularly given work-from-home status. Meloxicam prescribed to help reduce swelling.
